entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: EMA recommends authorisation of Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer
entries.description: EMA’s human medicines committee (CHMP) has recommended granting a marketing authorisation in the European Union for Rasonque (daraxonrasib), an oral treatment for adults with…
entries.summary: EMA recommends marketing authorization for Rasonque for metastatic pancreatic cancer.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to prepare for EU marketing authorization and regulatory submissions for this small‑molecule therapy.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Health Canada launches pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials: Notice
entries.description: Health Canada launches a pilot for select academic-led pediatric standard of care clinical trials.  If the criteria for the pilot are met and the trial is accepted under the pilot, sponsors will not be expected to comply with all of the regulatory requirements.
entries.summary: Health Canada has launched a pilot that reduces regulatory requirements for academic-led pediatric standard-of-care clinical trials when certain criteria are met.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams managing pediatric academic studies need to monitor the new compliance expectations and adjust their oversight accordingly.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register of innovative drugs has been established under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must be aware of the register to identify which products qualify as innovative drugs and ensure appropriate submissions and compliance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Qualifying notice for Hernexeos (304237)
entries.description: A Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) is authorization to market a drug (i.e. a Notice of Compliance (NOC)), with the condition that the Sponsor undertake additional studies to verify the clinical benefit. Health Canada issues the NOC under section C.08.004 of the Food and Drug Regulations for a submission that qualifies under the Guidance Document: Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c).
entries.summary: Health Canada granted a Notice of Compliance with Conditions (NOC/c) for Hernexeos, requiring the sponsor to conduct additional studies to verify clinical benefit.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must plan and execute these additional studies and monitor compliance, as the product remains eligible for market access only under the NOC/c conditions.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA clarifies the PIP compliance verification procedure and paediatric rewards.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams need to understand the updated verification steps to ensure compliance and to access paediatric incentives.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: Data extracts of the Notice of Compliance database are now available as compressed ASCII text files.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to be aware of the new format for retrieving and integrating NOC data.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot becomes a permanent initiative starting January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across all therapeutic areas should incorporate the now-permanent ACT EU advice service into their clinical trial application planning and preparation processes.

entries.summary: No specific changes provided

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: The guide provides instructions for market authorization holders on reporting drug shortages and discontinuations under specific sections of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow these instructions to comply with regulatory reporting requirements for all product types.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide provides instructions for drug establishment licence holders on distributing Canadian-market drugs for consumption or use outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must ensure their distribution plans align with the guidance when exporting Canadian drugs, impacting licensing and compliance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance for drug establishment licence holders on exceptional importation and sale of drugs during shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations to legally import and sell drugs under exceptional circumstances.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: This guide explains how to extend expiration dates of marketed drugs to mitigate drug shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must follow the new guidance to ensure compliant expiration date extensions for marketed products.

entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: EMA releases procedural advice for applicants using the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams applying centrally must review the updated guidance to ensure compliance with EMA processes.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: The Drug Product Database extract files now provide complete product information for all approved, marketed, and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant, and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must be aware that the DPD data extract now includes all product types, affecting data management and compliance checks for all regulated products.

entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: End-of-year submission dates for type I variations in 2026 are advised.
entries.why_it_matters: MA holders seeking 2026 outcomes must submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings by these dates.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle
entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…
entries.summary: Global regulators have called for the accelerated adoption of alternatives to animal testing throughout the medicine development lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams across all therapeutic areas should be aware of this policy shift and begin evaluating or integrating non‑animal testing strategies in their development plans.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change
entries.description: By the end of 2026, EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap to help drive decisive change on how women’s health is considered across medicines development and regulation. This…,         Women are still missing: from research and data, prevention, diagnosis and treatment. But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…
entries.summary: EMA will develop a regulatory roadmap to better include women’s health in medicines development by the end of 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that future regulations will require consideration of women’s health throughout the development process.

entries.summary: The Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications has been updated to include new listings of drugs under sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review the updated register to ensure all relevant products are correctly recorded and compliant with supplementary protection certificate requirements.

entries.summary: Member states now provide contact points to review national implementation of QR codes for veterinary medicinal products authorised via CP, MRP, DCP and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware of these points to coordinate compliance checks for QR code implementation.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams handling clinical trials must now follow the updated process for CHMP‑requested GCP inspections, impacting preparation and documentation for all trial sites.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should review the updated list to determine if any of their products are affected and adjust monitoring accordingly.

entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary regulatory affairs teams must adjust residue monitoring and compliance procedures for these excluded substances.

entries.summary: MHRA launched a new Regulatory Advice Service for medical devices in December 2025.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams developing or working with medical devices can now schedule direct consultations with MHRA to clarify regulatory requirements.

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must update their pharmacovigilance procedures for veterinary products to remain compliant.
